Soft-tissue navigation is highly dependent on non-rigid registration. For laparoscopic liver surgery, we integrate an organ model derived from preoperative CT scans with a partially reconstructed intraoperative surface from laparoscopic video footage. The complexity of this task arises from insufficient intraoperative data, poor image quality, real-time processing needs, and the absence of material properties in CT scans. The registration process begins with coupling a finite element model to preoperative CT images, creating a trained biomechanical model of the organ. During surgery, the operator captures the organ's surface, and an optimization procedure finds the initial position and mechanical state that best matches the observed intraoperative views. The trained biomechanical model streamlines this process by limiting possible deformations, reducing the demand for dense intraoperative volume reconstruction, and bypassing the need to estimate material properties.

For a static, spherically symmetric spacetime, research has focused on conformal matter collineations within the energy-momentum tensor. The overall structure of these collineations is determined under non-degenerate conditions, with fifteen distinct, independent forms found. However, when the energy-momentum tensor becomes degenerate, the associated conformal collineations exhibit infinite degrees of freedom. Moreover, specific degenerate subcases may still harbor non-degenerate Ricci inheritance collineations.

Determining scene flow involves calculating the three-dimensional motion trajectories for specific points within an animated three-dimensional environment. Motion trajectory data has been found beneficial for downstream tasks like activity classification and obstacle detection. Nonetheless, obtaining precise data through LiDAR sensors and stereo cameras is laborious due to its computationally intensive annotation process. We address this issue by presenting a 3D scene flow benchmark along with a novel self-supervised training framework that enables a flow estimator to learn accurate data without explicit flow label training. We establish the BFS-flow dataset as our benchmark, featuring complex real-world environments and diverse motion patterns across 7,170 video clips with 21 million sampled points. Furthermore, we develop a self-supervised training framework that automatically generates flow labels by regenerating virtual scenes based on predicted foreground and background elements. We evaluate our framework's performance on the BFS-flow dataset, achieving state-of-the-art results using only self-generated labels.

In recent years, AI networks, specifically those based on artificial neural systems, have significantly outperformed competitors in a wide range of tasks including image recognition, sound analysis, and language interpretation. However, widespread use of such models was previously hindered due to their massive computational requirements for both initial training and operational deployment. Neuromorphic computing technology, which allows bio-realistic neural networks to operate at high speeds while minimizing energy consumption, has now become an appealing substitute. We present a proposal to utilize a Random Neural Network as a versatile classifying model that combines the high accuracy of traditional ML models and the efficiency of neuromorphic systems. This approach involves converting input data into a series of sparse, time-based signals and using a simple neural system with binary components for both classification and subsequent processing. We successfully applied this method to real-world datasets for mammal and fruit classification, obtaining satisfactory accuracy levels of 98.4% and 99.1% respectively, and were able to process numerous samples in rapid succession while consuming extremely low amounts of electrical energy.

This research investigates the thermodynamic characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark matter under a strong magnetic field at finite temperature, applying the MIT bag model. Furthermore, we derived the equation of state for spin-polarized strange quark matter in the presence of a strong magnetic field, and subsequently, we examined the structure of spin-polarized strange quark stars across varying temperatures and magnetic fields.

A Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property in a graph implies that each perfect matching can be combined with another to create a Hamiltonian cycle. This concept was first introduced by Las Vergnas in 1979. Our research aims to explore which cubic graphs with a Perfect-Matching-Hamiltonian property also possess the 2-factors-with-a-Hamiltonian-cycle property. Our key findings indicate that nearly all such graphs exhibit the 2-factors-property, specifically those graphs whose edges can be properly 3-colored. The significance of this theorem is highlighted by a comparable result previously established for T-bridged cubic graphs. Furthermore, a proper 2-factor coloring of a graph is equivalent to partitioning its edges into two-factorful pairs, which implies that every two factor can be combined with another to create a Hamiltonian cycle. As a result, we obtain the corresponding result for graphs that admit a proper 3-edge coloring.

Recent research on block designs by Amarra, Devillers, and Praeger, involving specific quadratic polynomials, shows potential connections to two influential conjectures. The Bunyakovsky Conjecture would yield a crucial implication - infinitely many instances of the required designs. A vast number of prime values of the involved polynomials have been found and their quantities match closely the expectations based on a refined variant of the Bateman-Horn Conjecture. Although the infinite prime values of the polynomials have yet to be definitively confirmed, the results provide significant support for both the Bunyakovsky and Bateman-Horn Conjectures.

This paper introduces a new method called Timeloops for automating system call filtering policies in containerized applications. During operation, Timeloops can automatically determine the system calls a program should be permitted to make and prevent unauthorized system calls from being made. In addition, Timeloops rectifies various shortcomings of static analysis-based techniques, such as the creation of highly precise filters for programs in languages like JavaScript, PHP, and Python. Developed using standard, reliable technologies, Timeloops features a simple and efficient design comprising less than 500 lines of code. Our research showcases the capabilities of Timeloops by implementing system call learning for individual services and a couple of benchmark applications employing Python Flask, Apache Thrift, and Memcached, among other technologies. Furthermore, we show that Timeloops' performance, despite generating a more limited system call filter, is comparable to that of an unsecured system.

Investigating global $B-L$ symmetry within the Standard Model is necessary due to the anomaly cancellation requirements which necessitate three right-handed neutrinos that enable the natural generation of small Standard Model neutrino masses through the seesaw mechanism. Within an extension of the Standard Model featuring a $B-L$ symmetry, we introduce a pseudo-Goldstone boson dark matter framework where the imaginary component of a complex $B-L$ Higgs field constitutes the dark matter present in the universe. The universe's dark matter abundance is dictated by the Standard Model Higgs boson-mediated process, yet its interaction with nucleons via the exchange of Higgs bosons is heavily suppressed due to its pseudo-Goldstone nature. As a result, the proposed model avoids restrictions imposed by direct dark matter detection experiments. Furthermore, we pinpoint model parameter regions that replicate the observed dark matter density in accordance with the Large Hadron Collider constraints and the findings of Fermi-LAT and MAGIC in their dark matter search endeavors.

This study develops a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter where target appearance probabilities are organized on a grid. A streamlined variation of the Rao-Blackwellized point mass filter predicts the density of unobserved targets within grid cells using sum-of-Gaussians representations. The filter's dynamics and measurement updates are applied to both targets within the grid and those outside. Notably, the filter retains closed-form solutions for the first two statistical moments of the unobserved targets' density, outside the grid. A simulation demonstrates the filter's efficiency in tracking multiple targets with reduced computational expenses, governed by the level of noise in sensor data. Furthermore, a basic sensor management approach leverages the filter's estimate of unobserved targets' density within the grid, with goals of maximizing targets detection probabilities at minimal cost. The concept of equivalent isotropic targets within the grid leads to a basic objective function for sensor cost, with potential applications to sensor selection, scheduling, and network formation.

This study examines the null controllability of a population model that includes an interior degenerate diffusion component. By first establishing a new Carleman estimate for the adjoint system in its entirety, and subsequently deriving a relevant observability inequality, we aim to demonstrate the existence of a localized control action capable of driving the population towards extinction within a finite time frame.

The dynamic environment of soccer games poses a significant challenge for robots due to its unpredictable nature, making it an ideal test bed for developing advanced perception and decision-making capabilities. In this paper, we focus on a specific soccer scenario where three or more humans play soccer against a team of robots in possession of the ball, aiming to score a goal. To achieve this, we employ deep reinforcement learning to optimize the actions of the robots for both shooting and passing. Our objective is to create passing and shooting policies that give the highest probability of scoring. Through experiments conducted in simulation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by successfully scoring goals after just 150 training matches, utilizing real 3D scans of a soccer field. Furthermore, we show the efficiency and robustness of our method by achieving passes and goals in less than five seconds, and we make our implementation publicly available for further research and collaboration.

High-resolution subsurface modeling via seismic imaging has the potential to be greatly improved with Full Waveform Inversion (FWI).  However, FWI can become trapped in local minima due to its nonlinear optimization nature. Two alternatives, Wavefield Reconstruction Inversion (WRI) and Extended Source Waveform Inversion (ESI), have been proposed as methods to improve seismic imaging. Both of these methods relax the strict adherence to wave equation accuracy found in FWI and instead, WRI and ESI introduce non-physical source concepts that match observed data with synthetic data generated using extended sources. Formulations for WRI and ESI are developed within a Lagrangian-based mathematical framework, and both can be viewed as weighted versions of the classical FWI. Conjugate gradient methods are also explored, with an escaled residual formulation proposed for ESI. The effectiveness of these methods is demonstrated through synthetic examples, specifically in terms of computational cost and final image quality.

We've developed an all-optical technique for producing optical nonreciprocity on a microchip, achieved through the process of quantum squeezing a specific mode in coupled resonator systems. A key factor in this method involves applying classical coherent light in a one-way fashion to parametrically pump a nonlinear resonator. This selective pumping induces a chiral interaction between photons within the resonators, allowing us to build optical diodes and quasi-circulators. Notably, this technique allows for the isolation of intense red-light signals by more than 40 dB, while also enabling the precise control of light transmission in optical circuits using control photons.

We have presented the results from the AstroSat analysis of the high-mass X-ray binary X-ray pulsar IGR J19294+1816 during its Type-I outburst in October 2019. Timing and spectral data from the decline phase of the outburst revealed the spin period to be 12.485 seconds, with significant spectral features. A Quasi Periodic Oscillation was observed at a frequency of 0.003 Hz and an RMS amplitude of 0.24 Hz during higher states of the system, disappearing as the system moved to lower states. Our results also indicate the presence of a broad cyclotron line in the lower states, located at 29.4 ± 1.4 keV, from which the magnetic field strength was calculated as 2.79 ± 0.13 x 10^12 Gauss. Observations place the inner radius of the accretion disc at 1.35 +/- 0.15 stellar radii, outside the magnetic sphere of influence, indicating the accretion process occurs through an outer accretion disc, with a power spectrum analysis highlighting 1/f noise properties in higher states of the system.

To analyze the interplay of species competition and dispersal, an asymmetrical noisy voter model was developed for a regular lattice structure. The model allows one species to colonize nearest-neighbor sites, while another species can settle at any distance but is less successful in doing so. The model includes external noise, which can lead to random species swaps in the lattice. The combination of these dynamics results in various species competition outcomes, including the exclusion of one species, distinct population coexistence, or bistable coexistence dependent on the starting population ratio. The model shows that an abrupt transition occurs as immigration intensity surpasses a critical point, causing the irreversible decline of the species with shorter dispersal range due to a cusp catastrophe leading to half loop dynamics.

Ancient sundials served as primary timekeepers before the invention of mechanical clocks, with the classical Islamic civilization utilizing the Sun's daily movement to determine prayer times, often relying on sundials for this purpose. This knowledge eventually spread to Indonesia through Islamic cultural influences. Indonesian sundials developed as a reflection of local advancements in astronomy, technology, art, and architecture, with historical examples warranting detailed documentation and study, though often overlooked in existing literature. To collect necessary spatial and temporal information on these sundials, a citizen science initiative could be implemented, addressing research inquiries while promoting science education among the general public. This concept has been proposed as a framework, referred to as the Suryakala-Nusantara program, to explore sundials through citizen science methods.

This research focuses on an integrated data and energy transmission network, which incorporates D2D communication. This hybrid network allows a central hub to transfer data to those in need and supply power to those who require it. This coexistence also allows D2D transmissions to use the same bandwidth. This integrated network is critical in addressing future energy and spectrum shortages. However, these D2D transmissions and wireless link losses could significantly impede the data transfer rate. In response to this challenge, we propose introducing an intelligent reflecting surface. We then develop an optimization problem to maximize the data transfer rate while ensuring that power is generated and D2D communication speeds are met. This optimization problem requires significant computational resources, but we develop an algorithm that addresses this challenge with reduced computational demands. Finally, simulations confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

The surge in telework needs has highlighted the potential benefits of fully
automating and controlling experiments remotely. This work presents the technical
advancements of creating a two-dimensional LDV measurement system using a single-
point LDV system via a remotely controllable and automated setup. The document's
aim is to expedite the development of similar setups for this kind of application,
which is highly versatile and can be applied to various scenarios including both
air-based acoustic signal-driven samples and mechanically induced samples.

The effectiveness of programmable electrostatic phase plates is subject to debate 
given their varying suitability for particular applications. Our study delves into 
alternative designs of phase plates specifically tailored to mitigate spherical 
aberration in Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEMs). Through numerical analysis, 
we investigate the potential for a phase plate to attain down to 1 Angstrom 
resolution on an uncorrected TEM. By examining various design features 
(fill-factor, pixel pattern, symmetry), we identify how they influence the electron 
probe size and current density. Our proposed designs exhibit probe sizes ($d_{50}$) 
as low as 0.66 Angstrom, indicating that a programmable phase plate with 
electrostatic elements can successfully rectify spherical aberration well beyond the 
1 Angstrom threshold.

The success of data-driven dialogue models heavily relies on their ability to accurately encode user input to generate relevant and effective responses. While it is common to evaluate the generated text for its semantic and syntactic quality, the underlying representation of this encoding is often overlooked, which can hinder the model's performance in anticipating the next utterance. This work argues that merely assessing text generation metrics is insufficient for ensuring that the encoder representations effectively capture necessary information for dialogue comprehension, thus proposing a set of evaluation tasks to examine these internal representations and analyzing how they compare to those of standalone language models. Our experiments indicate that the encoder representations extracted from the generative dialogue model perform significantly better than those from the corresponding generative language model in certain evaluation tasks, suggesting that the context-deriving encoder components of the generative model differ from those in a standalone language model and are optimized for text generation rather than meaning. The proposed framework of representing and assessing encoder representations is believed to be a valuable addition to the field of natural language processing and machine learning.

Deep learning methods for LiDAR data analysis have revolutionized 3D place recognition in autonomous vehicles and robotics by improving local re-localization and loop-closure detection rates in complex environments. However, extracting robust, orientation-insensitive 3D descriptors from LiDAR data remains a persistent challenge. To tackle this, this research introduces a novel, range-based, deep learning network called AttDLNet that leverages an attention mechanism to selectively emphasize contextual and inter-feature connections. The proposed network is tested and validated on the KITTI dataset, with experimental results showing its enhanced performance and loop-closure capabilities when incorporating attention layers. The study indicates that adding this attention mechanism yields more efficient loop closures and outperforms existing LiDAR-based place recognition approaches. Moreover, results suggest that encoder layers with middle depths exhibit the best mean performance and exhibit robustness to orientation variations, with code publicly available for review and replication.

Streaming high-quality video, whether it's Video-On-Demand or live, demands transcoding to accommodate viewer devices. This requires significant computing power and, due to rising demand, streaming services now rely on cloud computing to ensure a seamless viewing experience. Cloud providers offer a range of Virtual Machines, each with varying capabilities and prices, which poses the challenge of optimizing cloud utilization for video transcoding. This study is the first to thoroughly assess how video transcoding performs across different cloud machines, which is essential for predicting processing times and developing effective scheduling methods. Based on this analysis and the cost variability of cloud machines, the research provides a model that helps evaluate the suitability of each cloud machine for different transcoding tasks. This model can provide resource provisioning with the best balance of performance and cost, thus enhancing the efficient use of cloud services for video streaming.

We have derived a semi-analytical formula for the dynamic density-density correlation of massless Dirac electrons in doped graphene, which is applicable at finite temperatures. This finding is key to understanding the thermal screening of interactions among Dirac electrons and we leverage it to calculate the thermal capacity and compressibility of doped graphene. Notably, at very low temperatures, the thermal capacity displays a linear temperature dependence characteristic of normal Fermi liquids, with the coefficient controlled by the velocity of charge carriers in the material.

Continuous speech leads to consistent prosody patterns, yet current speech synthesis models often disregard context. These systems fall short when it comes to producing high-quality paragraphs, necessitating a system that integrates contextual information. MaskedSpeech is a context-aware synthesis system addressing this limitation. By building upon a masking strategy, MaskedSpeech incorporates contextual acoustic cues into each sentence, enabling a more natural intonation. Additionally, cross-sentence semantic information is incorporated into the speaker's embedding, allowing for a more coherently expressed intonation. Furthermore, MaskedSpeech employs a multi-task learning approach to enhance semantic sentence encoding, incorporating total regression loss and contrastive loss. Experimental results on the Mandarin MegaSentence dataset indicate an improvement in MOS scores by 0.3 and IntonEval scores by 0.07 compared to the baseline.

We provide explicit definitions for the spectral and orbital stability of solitary waves in a model that includes a Klein-Gordon equation and an anharmonic oscillator. We also conduct a comprehensive analysis of the linearized equation's spectrum at the solitary wave state.

Q-ball studies in a single symmetry theory are common, yet the field can be more expansive, allowing for the examination of theories featuring multiple symmetries in a more general context. In this paper, we explore this broader scenario, analyzing both the standard and advanced limits within this theoretical framework and identifying essential conditions for existence in the more complex scenarios. Additionally, we identify a previously unexamined Q-ball state, which we term 'cored', and demonstrate that it could possess stability under specific conditions; a more detailed investigation into its implications will be addressed in a subsequent study.

We investigated a cyclic universe containing holographic dark energy with different infrared cutoffs, excluding the Big Rip singularity. The study reveals that, in the absence of interaction between the cosmos sectors, the HDE model using the Hubble radius cutoff behaves like a cosmological constant within cyclic cosmology. Furthermore, we discovered that cyclic patterns of contraction and expansion may occur for both interacting and non-interacting universes, provided that the Granda-Oliveros cutoff is selected for the HDE's energy density.

Gnutzmann and Smilansky previously developed a formula for the bond scattering matrix of a graph using a Hermitian matrix, for which an alternative proof has been devised, employing a method related to the zeta function of a graph. Furthermore, the formula has been broadened to cover regular coverings of graphs, and a novel 'L-function' concept for graphs has been defined, yielding a determinant expression. This has a corresponding outcome where the extended Gnutzmann and Smilansky formula can be represented by the graph's 'L-functions'.

We derive new conclusions regarding the additive Galois module properties of specific wildly ramified finite non-abelian extensions of Q. Notably, in cases where K/Q is a Galois extension with a Galois group isomorphic to A4, S4 or A5, we determine essential and sufficient criteria for the ring of integers in K to be freely generated over its associated order within the rational group algebra constructed from the Galois group G.

In experiments involving particle collisions, identifying neutral long-lived particles relies on either finding decay products at unusual locations or missing energy. The choice between these methods depends on the particle's properties, specifically its decay probability and the ease of detecting its decay products. To decide which method is most effective, researchers can refer to an effective area that combines both concepts. This effective area represents the fraction of such particles that are either detected through their displaced origins or registered as invisible based on their decay products or missing energy. The effective area can also be understood as the sum of displaced and invisible detection probabilities, weighted by a correlation factor accounting for particles that meet both criteria. An illustration of this effective area as a function of the particle's decay length is provided for two types of two-body decays involving an bottom anti-baryon. This illustration has significant implications for future studies of these particles at the Belle and Belle II experiments.

This study provides a detailed examination of the potential inaccuracies in
the output of contextualized language models when analyzing diachronic semantic
shifts in word meanings. We present an enhanced ensemble method that surpasses
earlier contextualized approaches and apply it to investigate the levels of
semantic change in English vocabulary over the course of 5 decades. Our
results show that contextualized methods may inaccurately predict significant
change in words with little to no actual semantic evolution, or whose
status remains unclear. These difficult cases are scrutinized, along with
suggested categorizations, to better understand words with ambiguous or
contested diachronic trajectories.

Active galactic nuclei (AGNs), containing accreting black holes at their center, allow for the investigation of black hole mass and spin through the analysis of electromagnetic spectra. This research uses the Spin-Modified Fundamental Plane of black hole activity, a non-linear model that links radio luminosity, optical or X-ray luminosity, black hole mass, and spin. Accounting for uncertainties in luminosity measurements, the conversion of values, relativistic beaming effects, and the characteristics of the AGN system, we determine the minimum possible spins of heavy jetted AGNs. These results help explore the relationship between the masses of ultra-light scalar, vector, and tensor particles, closing a gap in parameter space around $10^{-20}-10^{-19}$eV. Additionally, we determine the upper limits on the decay length of axion-like particles due to photon regeneration, limited by the observed jet lengths in AGNs, and further constrain the decay length to $<1.5\times 10^{12}$m for photons with masses less than $10^{-20}$eV.

A distinctive feature of neural development is the rhythmic shifting of cell nuclei
between the upper and lower layers of the neuroepithelial tissue as interkinetic nuclear
migration (IKNM) unfolds. In this study, we utilize extended, high-speed lightsheet and two-photon imaging
techniques in live zebrafish retinas during initial development to gain insights into the underlying mechanisms governing
the behavior of cell nuclei during IKNM. Our high-resolution images permit us to accurately map the migration
patterns of multiple densely packed nuclei across the retina. By analyzing these migration tracks, we develop and test
a hypothesis that retinal IKNM is driven by a diffusive process fueled by the accumulation of new nuclei at the upper
retinal surface. Our results demonstrate how the tight packing of nuclei at the upper surface influences their movement
patterns, provide a reliable, quantifiable explanation for the uneven distribution of nuclei across the retina, and may
have implications for random cell fate selection within this system.

In various image processing tasks, including video compressed sensing and color image demosaicing, images must be separated from coded measurements that represent their superposition. Real-world code patterns, which often contain code arrays with consecutive ones in the measurement matrix, typically result in poor reconstruction performance due to excessive correlation. Although code optimization techniques, such as orthogonal code design, generally yield favorable results, they usually neglect code pattern constraints and frequently require costly optimization processes, such as semidefinite relaxation, to be computed. In this paper, we introduce a novel code optimization model, specifically tailored to address the challenge of separating code patterns and computational constraints in the measurement matrix. The proposed model is solved through the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), which allows the model to be efficiently computed. The proposed model's performance is consistently better than that of existing code patterns, as well as other optimized codes designed to facilitate separation, in both compressed video reconstruction and image demosaicing applications, allocating fewer erroneous elements per measurement and providing stable performance across different compressed sensing ratios.

We've developed a comprehensive hydrodynamic theory that applies to polar active fluids in the presence of randomly distributed inclusions, and our model demonstrates the possibility of overcoming these obstructions to maintain a non-zero overall speed. Contrary to previous assumptions, the dynamics of this specific class of active matter cannot be accurately captured using simplified hydrodynamic models when the spatial environment is two-dimensional up to five-dimensional space; however, we were able to derive precise, dimension-dependent scaling parameters for these dimensions.

Researchers within the same institution often rely on their institutional email as their primary means of communication. Due to their accessibility and private data storage, these emails are vulnerable to cyber threats and can serve as lucrative targets. Our proposed approach aims to examine research institutions' internal communication networks for potential security breaches. Initially, we gathered and analyzed email data from multiple research institutions, including three in Spain and one in Portugal. We applied an SEIR complex network dynamics model to simulate and assess the vulnerability of these networks. Our results indicated that a significant proportion of email accounts have experienced security breaches, while more than 90% of network nodes exhibit susceptibility to cyber threats. Our research can facilitate the enhancement of email account security for research institutions, while also opening up avenues for further exploration in the realm of communication security. Due to confidentiality considerations, we cannot disclose the source from which we acquired the communication network data, as this would reveal sensitive information.

Inspired by the pseudogap phenomenon in cuprates, we propose a new idea, 
the concept of an "exceptional" van Hove singularity, where a strong 
electron interaction fragments a continuous Fermi surface into disjoint regions. 
We identify this singularity with the merging of two separated Fermi surface 
segments, and demonstrate that it is close to a van Hove singularity, 
reaching it by adjusting a material parameter affecting its dispersion. 
We assert that, in the broader family of cuprate materials, 
the onset of pseudogap is attainable solely through inducing this exceptional 
van Hove singularity, and that this results in a distinct Lifshitz 
transition distinguished by heightened heat capacity and a nematic susceptibility, 
both consistent with empirical observations.

This paper details a specialized apparatus built for use in Aberdeen Tunnel's laboratory in Hong Kong. The laboratory is uniquely situated to study spallation neutrons produced by cosmic-ray muons with 611 meters of water equivalent in depth. The apparatus consists of six layers of horizontal plastic-scintillator detectors that pinpoint the direction and location of incoming muons. Between these layers, a neutron sensor filled with 650 kilograms of liquid scintillator containing a gadolinium dopant significantly enhances detection efficiency of the produced spallation neutrons. Additionally, we discuss the performance characteristics of this apparatus.

Ground-based observations of planetary movements are crucial in validating the findings of space-based missions like Kepler and TESS. Although these missions show that planets are widespread, the success of these missions relies heavily on the use of transit photometry and ground-based radial velocity surveys to determine the physical properties of these celestial bodies. The TESS telescope is capable of identifying planets around bright nearby stars, which are ideal candidates for follow-up observations. We propose the TESS-Keck Survey to investigate various properties of these exoplanets. Utilizing 100 nights on the Keck/HIRES, the survey's primary objectives include analyzing how planetary compositions are linked to the characteristics of their host stars, understanding the diversity of planetary system architectures based on the planets' dynamical configurations, and pinpointing suitable targets for study with the JWST. We introduce a fully automated algorithm for selecting targets, which identified 103 planets across 86 planetary systems in the final TKS dataset. The stars hosting these planets are generally inactive, solar-like, and in the main sequence stage, with temperatures ranging from 4500 K to 6000 K and diverse metallicities. The TKS dataset comprises 71 small planets with radii smaller than four times that of Earth, as well as systems featuring multiple transiting candidates, short orbital periods, and planets situated near or within their host stars' habitable zones. The target selection strategy described can be adapted to facilitate the comparison of observational data

The growth of Information Technology has significantly altered how information is shared, making it necessary to convert printed documents into digital formats.  There has been an increase in fraudulent activities lately.  To prevent such account-related fraud, a system was devised which employs ID card extraction via OCR and NLP for verification purposes.  Optical Character Recognition, a technology that enables the conversion of images to text, can also be used to convert an Indonesian ID card or KTP into text format.  This facilitates easier data entry for service operators.  To enhance accuracy, the extracted text was further corrected using Natural Language Processing.  When tested using 50 Indonesian ID card images, the F-score achieved was 0.78, and the extraction process for each ID card took approximately 4510 milliseconds.

Quantum harmonic oscillators were computationally analyzed using two Monte Carlo techniques: molecular dynamics with a harmonic force and a Metropolis algorithm with their respective step sizes. Our evaluation of path integral sampling success hinged on comparing simulated results to established analytical solutions. Surprisingly, neither algorithm yielded perfect sample paths, but both achieved accurate macroscopic measurements of microcanonical quantities, including mean position, momentum, and kinetic energy. Furthermore, our experiment revealed that competing algorithms could produce equivalent outcomes even when employing disparate sampling methods. Consequently, this study highlights the essential role of performance benchmarks in assessing quantum harmonic oscillator simulators and suggests the framework's applicability to more complex systems.

The Yarkovsky-O'Keefe-Radzievskii-Paddack effect significantly impacts the rotational states of small asteroids by exerting a net torque resulting from solar radiation reflected and re-emitted by the surface. As a consequence of this phenomenon, the rotation period of these asteroids gradually changes, which can be best measured through light curves as the phase shift accumulates over time in a quadratic manner. To study this effect in detail, researchers collected archival data and conducted new photometric observations for asteroids 1992 SK, Geographos, and Toro, before utilizing a light curve inversion method to match their shapes and rotation characteristics. By modeling the YORP effect and incorporating other relevant parameters into their analysis, scientists were able to detect the YORP acceleration in three asteroids and found that the YORP acceleration in all ten detected cases was positive, accelerating their rotations. Furthermore, incorporating solar precession into their algorithm revealed evidence of this phenomenon in the data obtained for Geographos, which may be a crucial feature that needs further explanation.

The youth are increasingly relying on Instagram as a source of information, with political figures leveraging the platform to disseminate opinions and agendas. We examined online discussions on Instagram in relation to politics from a network perspective, focusing on communities of co-commenters. Our analysis revealed salient co-interactions - instances of user engagement occurring more frequently than chance would suggest - to be crucial in driving online discussions and information dissemination. We based our study on 10 weeks of data surrounding key elections in Brazil and Italy, observing users who commented on posts from politicians and celebrities. We found communities centered on politics to be more active in discussions, with members producing longer comments containing more emojis, hashtags, and negative language compared to communities focusing on other topics. Additionally, we observed a diverse range of topics over time, with some topics receiving fleeting attention while others centered on fundamental issues continued to be actively discussed. Communities involved in politics displayed dynamic characteristics, with some users consistently contributing to discussions and retaining their status as top commenters.

We show that any subgroup of homeomorphisms of a compact surface that fix the boundary, whose action within the surface's interior is highly transitive, cannot be topologically compact when using the compact-open topology's inherited structure.

Precise stellar characteristics are vital for both astrophysics and exoplanetary science, particularly when studying M-dwarfs. Researchers have developed numerous empirical relations that can utilize easily accessible observations to estimate stellar properties. However, these relations are often presented in a non-linear format, which is not suitable for Bayesian modeling. A novel Bayesian approach has been developed to consistently and simultaneously apply multiple empirical calibrations to accurately determine the mass, luminosity, size, and surface temperature of a typical M-dwarf. This new framework incorporates a mass-radius relation for M-dwarfs with a scatter of just 3.1% at fixed mass. The researchers also established the M-dwarf Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Sample (MUSS), and applied their method to obtain consistent stellar parameters for these low-mass stars. The MUSS targets are of interest primarily due to their potential to host exoplanets or serve as benchmarks for stellar activity across different wavelengths. Using the field MUSS stars, a mass range for low-mass stars in the solar neighborhood was established through a controlled analysis. Additionally, a straightforward method based on mass was used to derive additional stellar parameters, and the resulting relations for M-dwarfs yielded a 0.04 dex discrepancy with more rigorous analyses based on spectral energy distributions. A new, transparent, and reproducible analysis code was also released to allow other studies to derive consistent stellar parameters.

Confining modes at the edge of a two-dimensional material generate line waves that travel along the perimeter, offering valuable properties in the infrared to visible light spectrum.  These waves can be constrained in a closed loop or guided along any two-dimensional path using appropriate boundaries, and possess valuable applications in on-chip communications and quantum systems.  Our research demonstrates the use of a two-layered metasurface to constrict and steer line waves generated by a graphene monolayer in visible light.  Each layer of the metasurface transforms the boundary conditions, and by manipulating the interaction between the layers, we can adjust the waves trajectorries.  Our theoretical model uses numerical simulations to validate the results, and we propose a scalable implementation for potential real-world use.

Although a key function in database management, query evaluation classification lacks comprehensive guidelines when dealing with self-joined queries. Our investigation aims to bridge this knowledge gap by examining how self-joins impact the complexity of enumerating database results, building on existing research. By extending two known categories of classification to incorporate self-joined queries with respect to efficiency, this study provides an in-depth analysis and illustrates potential enumeration strategies using self-joins. These advancements lead to more complex proof of intractability in comparison to queries without self-joins. Additionally, this study introduces an existing method to handle queries without optimization after a self-join and analyzes its complexity. For both efficient and intractable cases, our efficient enumeration methods provide quantitative measures of performance gains achievable through self-join optimization.

Multiple formal models can equivalently define functions that map infinite strings to other infinite strings, including MSO-transducers, streaming transducers, and certain two-way transducers. However, even when restricted to single passes through the input, some functions in these models can still be undecidable by Turing machines with infinite input, despite being defined by finite-state machines. To address this issue, a new decision-making approach is proposed for determining whether a specific function is computable and if so, to create a corresponding Turing machine. 

For the type of functions in question, being computable is equivalent to having a specific property called continuity. To efficiently assess continuity, a method is proposed using a finite approximation, which can be computed in PSPACE. This assessment approach proves to be useful in either proving continuity for functions that were previously only known to be continuous due to their representation, or in identifying undecidable functions that arise from the composition of continuous functions. 

In the case of Turing-computable functions, being continuous is also equivalent to having a specific stability property. Stability can be decided in PS^P, which implies that all continuous functions are also stable. Furthermore, several newly proven undecidable functions are presented as applications of these decision methods. These examples come from domains such as the comparison of equivalent regular expressions by a 2-way transducer, a binary encoding of non-empty regular languages recognized by a transducer, and a function that maps one regular language to another based on their relative sizes

Researchers have analyzed collision data with an integrated luminosity of 3 inverse femtobarns, and through amplitude analysis of specific two-body decay events, have discovered that the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons exhibits a higher fraction of longitudinal polarization than the $B^0_s$ decay to the same mesons. Furthermore, this difference in longitudinal polarization was utilized to determine the branching fraction of the $B^0$ decay to a pair of $K^*$ mesons.

A machine learning technique known as reservoir computing generates a model that mimics complex systems and can be trained on significantly smaller amounts of data compared to alternative methods. The latest version of this approach simplifies training by minimizing the need to adjust numerous parameters. In a recent experiment involving a highly complex system with distinct time scales and multiple coexisting patterns of behavior, a reservoir computer of the new design demonstrated several advantages over its traditional counterpart. Specifically, it used a much smaller amount of data for training, a much shorter time to adjust its performance, a smaller number of parameters to adjust, and a much higher level of accuracy in predicting patterns of behavior, even when those patterns change rapidly. In addition to this performance, it was able to predict areas of stability accurately, further confirming the benefits of this new algorithm.

A new bias-corrected estimator has been created for the mean absolute deviation of a median regression model, addressing the problem of irregularity that typically hinders conventional bias reduction.  To overcome this limitation, a specific alternative strategy was implemented.  Establishing the bias correction involves verifying the local asymptotic normality property and a specific Bahadur-Kiefer representation.  Developed within the context of a traditional asymptotic framework, this proposal appears to retain effectiveness in high-dimensional settings, as evidenced by simulation results.

To address scalability issues with Eulerian methods for finding optimal controllers under constraints and worst-case disturbances in variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs formulations, we've developed a second-order successive sweep algorithm for calculating the reachable state space. This approach, which assumes a continuous and smooth Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs equation, enables us to determine the states that can be reached within a given time frame under worst-case conditions and state feedback control.

Multi-Layer Perceptrons are particularly effective at generating accurate
low-dimensional representations of data, such as images, shapes and light
fields. Despite notable variations in their precision when processing regular
periodic data, this approach has not been extensively tested on random data.
In this report, we examine the generalization capabilities of such data- to
signal-processing neural networks within the context of SLAM. To enhance their
ability to handle periodic data and random data, we propose a neural network
architecture called MPA-Nets (Modulated Periodic Activations). MPA-Nets utilize
a shared network with periodic activation functions (such as sinusoidal or
tanh functions) to simultaneously model periodic signals within the range of one
period. Experimental results on regular and random data sets demonstrate the
superior generalization capabilities of MPA-Nets when compared to baseline
networks. Furthermore, applications of this approach in SLAM are explored,
including the use of range finders and the incorporation of inertial measurement
units, where its effectiveness in processing periodic data is clearly shown.

The underlying mechanisms of the ventral temporal cortex's animacy organization remain contentious, suggesting that animacy exists along a spectrum rather than a binary divide. Recent evidence suggests this continuum is influenced by the degree of presence or absence of distinct animal features or by how entities are perceived as social agents. In this study, a stimulus set with independent factors of visual categorizability and agency perception in animals was used to test these hypotheses through both computational neural networks and behavioral experiments. Utilizing functional magnetic resonance imaging, our findings showed that visual categorizability and agency perception separately explained independent components of the animacy spectrum in VTC. When combined, they fully captured the continuum, and our data indicated distinct posterior regions associated with each. The results of this study demonstrate the complex nature of the animacy spectrum in VTC, revealing multiple governing principles such as social agency that shape our understanding of this phenomenon.

The study proves the nonexistence of Landau-Siegel zeros or confirms quantum unique ergodicity for GL_2 Hecke-Maass newforms at a calculable speed, supporting 'effective' QUE for these forms. As a consequence, the distribution of low-lying zeros of the associated L-functions aligns with the predicted probability measure for a corresponding family of unitary matrices, providing partial confirmation of a conjecture by Keating and Sarnak regarding GL_3. The proof relies primarily on refining the convexity bound for second moments of L-functions in the conductor variable, contributed by the author.

We have adapted the quantum relational Hoare logic originally proposed in (Unruh, POPL 2019) to incorporate "expectations" into preconditions and postconditions, thereby enabling the quantification of pre-/postconditions that reflect the relationship between programs' inputs and outputs when comparing pairs of programs.

The rapid transmission of contagious diseases is frequently intensified by a single high-transmission event, a super-spreader occurrence. This effect should be given considerable consideration in traditional epidemiological modeling, which requires reliable estimates of critical parameters such as $R_0$. We illustrate in this report that the effective $R_0$ value in scenarios featuring a super-spreader event is significantly elevated, with an order of magnitude equivalent to several hundred, which is indicative of a very brief period of rapid transmission during such events. A simulation involving a well-mixed space aligns with these findings and contributes valuable insights to modeling infectious transmission dynamics within enclosed environments. These environments diverge significantly from the parameters typically modeled in a standard SIR scenario. The proposed model also yields expressions that relate $R_0$ values to physical and epidemiological variables in spaces featuring a super-spreader event. The results from the simulations and modeling point towards the vital importance of managing aerosolized pathogens transmitted via super-spreader events for the prevention of outbreaks.

Let's consider a complex topological vector space, denoted as X, along with the collection L(X) of continuous linear operators that act on X. This paper seeks to expand the concept of codiskcyclicity, initially developed for a solitary operator within L(X), to a broader context of operator sets defined as $\Gamma\subset L(X).$ Some key results regarding codiskcyclic collections of operators are proven, accompanied by a codiskcyclicity criterion. Furthermore, we demonstrate its practical utility by investigating the codiskcyclicity of C_0-semigroups comprised of operators.

The paper addresses the problem of bias in vector magnetic field maps, particularly in estimating the component perpendicular to the line-of-sight, Bperp. This issue has been identified previously, yet the precise mechanism behind Bperp's susceptibility to bias remains unclear, and existing mitigation methods prove ineffective. To delve deeper, we examined multiple data sources, including the SDO/HMI and SOLRA+ simulations, as well as several inversion techniques, both differential and nonlinear. Our investigation led to a key finding where the gap between Sp and magnetogram fills small-scale structures known as network holes, creating a distinct pattern. Comparing this pattern to additional features, we discovered that the difference between magnetogram data filled structures and actual magnetic fields takes the form of halos surrounding magnetic elements. Furthermore, we proved mathematically and visually that these halos possess near-zero net magnetic flux, and thus Bperp calculated from magnetogram data exhibit similar behavior. To test this, we manipulated the grid size of network holes and confirmed that reducing it to less than one pixel increases Bhalo calculations to negative values. To mitigate this bias, we suggest a straightforward and practical solution, and demonstrated its near-perfect magnetic flux accuracy through both simulated and real data instances, validating its broad applicability.

A comprehensive analysis has been conducted to measure the radii of 6097 young star clusters in 31 galaxies from the LEGUS survey. The custom analysis pipeline allowed for a large and contamination-resistant sample, giving us the largest dataset to date of its kind. The study discovered that the concentration of these star clusters varies significantly across different hosts, ranging from highly dispersed to tightly concentrated. Notably, the radii of these star clusters are unrelated to their individual masses or the global properties of their host systems when viewed through the lens of the specific density profile $\rho(r) \propto r^{-4}$, however, there are distinct patterns that do correlate, such as the radii increasing when observing the logarithm of the half-light as a function of surface density. The determined relationships will be crucial in future research as they establish a critical connection between stellar evolution and the dynamic behavior of galactic systems. The errors of the measurements are provided to allow for further statistical analysis and understanding.

We present a novel, direct method for lattice QCD calculations of light meson decays to two photons, specifically focusing on the $\eta_c \rightarrow 2\gamma$ process. This approach eschews the traditionally used effective theory, while still yielding a consistent result for the decay width $\Gamma(\eta_c \rightarrow 2\gamma) = 2.26(9) \, \textrm{keV}$ by leveraging LHCb data for a more precise outcome.

A sign problem encountered in Monte Carlo simulations beyond half-filling can be mitigated by transforming the integration path. However, this transformation introduces an additional computational cost associated with the Jacobian determinant in the Boltzmann weight, posing a significant barrier for large-scale simulations. Our proposed architecture, based on a novel application of complex-valued affine coupling layers in neural networks, efficiently circumvents this challenge by achieving linear scaling of the determinant cost. As a result, this method allows us to tackle intractably large systems plagued by a severe sign problem.

This paper examines the relationship between integers that are y-friable (or y-smooth) and the Dickman function. By assuming the Riemann Hypothesis (RH), we had a previous estimate of the count of y-friable integers up to x in terms of the Dickman function but it was limited to integers y greater than or equal to $(\log x)^{2+\varepsilon}$ due to previous work by Hildebrand and Saias. Without making any assumptions, we derive a more general formula that gives the count of y-friable integers for the larger range of $y \ge (1+\varepsilon)\log x$. This formula reveals a pattern that follows $x \rho(\log x/\log y)$ times correction factors. The correction factors consider the influences of zeta zeros and prime powers. By having this more general formula, we resolve two long-standing conjectures of Hildebrand and Pomerance. 

Hildebrand initially hypothesized that once $y$ is smaller than $(\log x)^{2+\varepsilon}$, the count of y-friable integers would no longer follow the estimated $x \rho(\log x/\log y)$ pattern, which we confirm to be true. 

As for Pomerance, he posed the question whether $\Psi(x,y) \ge x \rho(\log x/\log y)$ would always hold for all y greater than or equal to $e

Given any non-erasing free monoid morphism σ and subshift X, its image subshift Y under σ and the associated complexity functions p_X and p_Y exhibit the following relationship: there exist constants c, d, and C, where p_X scales by a factor of at least c times d, while scaling at most C, in the sufficiently large integers n in N. If σ is recognizable and letter-to-letter, then p_Y and p_X grow at similar rates, whereas if σ isn't letter-to-letter, there are instances where p_X isn't proportional to p_Y. As a result, topological entropy h_X isn't necessarily preserved when applying σ to X, indicating that defining topological entropy for free group currents F_N isn't feasible. Nevertheless, we can distinguish currents with or without zero or positive topological entropy.

By leveraging previously acquired skills and adapting them to unfamiliar tasks without explicit guidance, humans demonstrate impressive cross-task capabilities.
This study aims to enhance the cross-task generalization ability of massive language models in unsupervised settings, with a focus on models like T0 and FLAN.
We introduce a novel, unsupervised retrieval-augmentation method known as ReCross, which employs unlabeled samples to selectively draw from existing data, fine-tune the model for better performance.
The proposed method seamlessly integrates both high-efficiency dense retrieval and a more effective pair-wise re-ranking process to produce outstanding results, surpassing non-retrieval methods and alternative baselines in our experiments.

This research introduces the m-arcsinh Kernel ('m-ar-K') Fast Independent Component Analysis ('FastICA') approach ('m-ar-K-FastICA') for feature extraction, combining kernel-based dimensionality reduction with ICA to overcome the limitations of previous methods. Although the kernel trick offers a powerful way to tackle non-linearity, its effectiveness can be undermined by a lack of open-source and reproducible kernel implementations, especially in complex datasets. The proposed m-ar-K-FastICA approach uses a readily available and adaptable Python library that facilitates collaboration with scikit-learn, providing a more reliable solution for feature extraction even in data sets with high entropy levels and no need for data pre-whitening. Several classification experiments using open-access datasets from diverse domains have shown significant performance improvements, showcasing the enhanced capability of the proposed approach. Furthermore, a comparison with the established FastICA algorithm has validated its superiority in terms of reliability and efficiency.

This work offers an overview of requirements engineering in the gaming sector.
Existing research studies on this topic have been comprehensively examined.
Key characteristics of the gaming industry were identified and their connections to broader market dynamics discussed.
In addition, several potential areas for further research within this field were briefly highlighted.

Optimizing hyperparameters in the private version of the stochastic gradient descent algorithm is a critical issue due to limited access to private datasets for hyperparameter tuning. The development of algorithms that efficiently find optimal hyperparameters for a favorable balance between privacy and performance within a predetermined search space within an acceptable number of evaluations is crucial. In this paper, we introduce the first algorithm to achieve this within a reasonable complexity timeframe, specifically the Frank-Wolfe+DP-SGD method. The proposed algorithm swiftly identifies an optimal set of hyperparameters. The effectiveness and privacy-security of the method are demonstrated, particularly in its application to training a private convolutional neural network for image classification. The results highlight the method's ability to achieve high accuracy with robust privacy protection, with the potential for significant gains over previous standards.

For a Coxeter system denoted by (W,S), we develop the concept of a boolean complex consisting of involutions within W, mirroring Ragnarsson and Tenner's previous work. By applying discrete Morse theory, we identify the homotopy type of this boolean complex for a significant subset of Coxeter groups, including finite groups, revealing that its homotopy type is equivalent to that of a collection of spheres with dimension |S|-1. Moreover, we derive straightforward, recursive formulas to compute the number of spheres within this collection.

The Euclid satellite, set to launch in 2022, will significantly influence future cosmological research with its Visible and Near Infrared Spectrometer and Photometer instruments. The authors of this study analyzed how correlated readout noise affects in-flight measurements for the NISP detectors and proposed an analytical method for noise covariance matrices. Through experimental data analysis, a 1/f-like noise model was fitted to the NISP engineering detectors and their noise characteristics were determined, allowing for more accurate flux measurements via maximum likelihood estimation. It was found that using this approach, a four-fold decrease in measurement bias compared to the white noise model was possible. The authors conclude that even with the white noise model, negligible bias on NISP's in-flight measurements will be maintained, meeting Euclid's processing baseline requirements.

We applied an advanced statistical approach to examine the composition of 34,410 stars in the Milky Way disk using a vast dataset from the APOGEE-2. The study involved using a two-component model to break down elemental patterns into supernovae types and then comparing observed values to predicted values. The comparison yielded small discrepancies of up to 0.1 dex in some cases. The study revealed relationships between elements including a group sharing similar variations and distinct groups of elements with different behaviors. It also shed light on stars that the model struggled to accurately account for, likely indicating physical variations and small errors in measurements. Furthermore, the study enabled a simpler explanation of complex stellar patterns, a revised assessment of small differences in elemental patterns and a new way to investigate stellar puzzles known as "gaps". The study revealed that some of these gaps could be linked to changes in the rotation of the galaxy, while others required further investigation. Introducing a systematic framework to uncover similar phenomena and a method to visualize this on a scatter plot using dashed lines, the study was also used to examine the accuracy of the model in areas of [Fe/H] space and discovered that it performed better in certain regions, likely indicating the presence of stellar streams in other regions. The study was also used to explore the relationship between elements including [Ca/Fe] and [O/Fe] in different metallicity ranges, while a novel approach involving the grouping of elements into "families" led to a model

The COVID-19 pandemic spread globally in early 2020 and caused severe consequences in China, also exacerbating public health anxiety fueled by rampant online rumors. To address this pressing issue, we examined the dynamics of rumor propagation and proposed a method to measure the impact of a rumor by tracking the speed of its new adopters. Utilizing search frequency as a proxy for this metric, we identified the peak and attenuation coefficients which conform to an exponential distribution. Subsequently, we extracted the parameters of the Gaussian function to rank the influence of different rumors. Notably, government-led communication was found to accelerate the spread of a rumor, with its acceleration coefficient directly proportional to the increase in search frequency. In contrast, characteristics of the victim and lack of scientific understanding slowed down the spread, with their understanding of search frequency increasing at a rate equal to the peak coefficient minus the acceleration coefficient. These findings offer valuable insights for future pandemic prevention and control, as well as the management of public anxiety and rumor propagation. The proposed method not only validates its effectiveness through three典型案例 but also lays the groundwork for enhancing public health security in China and beyond.

A novel approach to measuring the distance to galaxies has been discovered by examining extragalactic planetary nebulae, specifically due to their nearly universal brightness pattern. Determining the precise distances to galaxies through planetary nebulae analysis depends on collecting comprehensive data sets, and the observed frequency of these nebulae directly correlates with the galaxies' overall mass. Therefore, researchers must either utilize wide-field observations or focus on the central areas of galaxies. By focusing on the central areas of elliptical galaxies within the Fornax cluster using near-infrared imaging of the H-alpha emission line, the H-Fornax3D project aims to establish an accurate and comprehensive distance measurement system. This will result in a comprehensive three-dimensional map of nebulae within thousands of galaxies, and in turn, facilitate a more accurate understanding of the evolution of planetary nebulae throughout the universe.

Every day, hospitals around the world gather vast amounts of physiological data from their patients, leading to an escalating interest in conducting statistical analyses to provide better medical diagnoses. These analyses involve complex computations on significant datasets, necessitating high-performance data processing systems that can balance efficiency and simplicity. To address the limitations of existing data processing solutions, we present \emph{LifeStream}, a robust stream processing engine specifically designed to handle physiological data efficiently. LifeStream optimizes performance while providing intuitive temporal query language support, thus striking a balance between ease of programming and computational speed. Furthermore, LifeStream exhibits superior performance, outperforming other leading stream processing engines and hand-tuned numerical libraries by up to $7.5\times$ and $3.2\times$ respectively, on realistic datasets and workload simulations.

This research paper confirms that certain types of curves, specifically those in higher dimensional space, do not fit the classification of Bertrand curves except in two-dimensional Euclidean space. A new category, called the timelike (1,3)-Bertrand curve, is defined to fill this gap and its characteristics are identified for curves in a four-dimensional Euclidean space.

The choice of loss function for a neural network is widely regarded as a key decision with far-reaching implications, given the numerous loss functions developed to date, making it crucial to carefully select one. Despite its significance, research on the topic often omits explicit justification for loss function selection. We contend that this lack of justification reflects an untested assumption prevalent within the deep learning community. In this research, we investigate how loss function impacts performance in a supervised classification context. Our findings reveal that certain, previously underappreciated loss functions, including the KL divergence, can yield superior outcomes compared to established methods, underscoring the need to view loss function choice as a parameter amenable to optimization, rather than a fixed constant.
A stabilizable boundary feedback controller is designed for the Navier-Stokes equations using a linear control scheme with an oblique boundary orientation.

This research aims to advance the understanding of thermomechanical behavior in polymer crystallization. Strain-induced crystallization plays a significant role in polymer mechanical and thermal properties and must be accounted for during production and final product application design. To effectively capture its mechanical and thermal impacts, the proposed model utilizes a unique decomposition approach to the deformation gradient and applies the Coleman--Noll procedure and minimum dissipation potential principle to material modeling. The resulting model includes suitable Helmholtz free energy and dissipation potential assumptions, which enables simulation of crystalline region formation, degradation, and temperature changes during cyclic loading tests. Numerical implementation based on the finite element method provides the basis for numerical solutions, which include simulations of material sample microstructure and temperature evolution.

To analyze the impact of external magnetization on doped Bi$_2$Se$_3$ with spin-triplet nematic superconductivity, we computationally investigate magnetic susceptibility in nematic and chiral superconducting states using the Ginzburg-Landau formalism near its critical temperature. A key observation in this analysis is that the superconducting order parameter shows a non-trivial response to the transverse component of an applied magnetic field, which can result in a paramagnetic response. Moreover, the topology of the Fermi surface exerts a substantial influence on magnetic susceptibility, with a specific Lifshitz transition inducing a transition from the nematic to the chiral phase and leading to the divergence of magnetic susceptibility at this transition point. Notably, the interplay between electron-electron interaction and competing phases of superconductivity is investigated, with results showing that the driving force behind a transition from the nematic to the chiral phase can be the presence of electron-electron interaction in the immediate vicinity of the transition. A comparison with existing experimental data is also presented in this analysis.

One significant issue in Imitation Learning (IL) is that obtaining perfect optimal demonstrations from a teacher is a challenging task due to the complexities involved, especially in robotics. Providing quality feedback is further constrained by the need to supply demonstrations for multiple state actions at once. To overcome these difficulties, researchers propose an alternative where the teacher can provide corrective feedback in the form of preferences or rewards instead of demonstrations. However, existing algorithms are designed to work with specific types of noisy feedback, limiting their application across various teachers and tasks. To tackle this problem, we suggest a different approach, one where we model a more flexible teacher who can provide both demonstrations and feedback in the form of preferences or rewards. We then develop a universal learning algorithm capable of adapting to this flexible teacher. By leveraging a novel data structure, the algorithm can integrate corrective feedback to accelerate its rate of learning from demonstrations. We support our algorithm's performance through theoretical analysis and experimental evidence, which also highlight the advantage of using corrective feedback compared to just demonstrations alone.

Continuous phase modulation detection using conventional differential detection techniques is highly resistant to various channel disturbances, such as phase and Doppler shift. Its basic structure makes it easy to implement, although it generates significant delay, limiting its data rate. The primary goal of this study is to minimize the delay differential detection scheme while preserving its resistance to channel phase. By analyzing the differential detection's performance through a coherent equivalent model, the proposed approach optimizes the delay parameter through maximum a posteriori estimation. Simulations demonstrate the existence of an optimal delay parameter and its influence on detection error rate. The proposed criterion is particularly relevant for deep learning-based CPM equalization methods.

New findings from 1D core-collapse simulations shed new light on the ultimate demise of massive stars, contradicting widely employed numerical models. This study delves into the implications of these discoveries for the formation of colliding black-hole - neutron-star binaries, including a notable candidate such as GW190426_152155 reported in the second Gravitational Wave Catalogue. Furthermore, it examines the influence of birth kicks and neutron-star sizes on the generation of these systems, as well as their potential to produce observable electromagnetic signals following the neutron-star's demise. Models derived from the newly discovered wind-driven collapse mechanism demonstrate that GW190426_152155 likely involved the merger of two black-holes, whereas a similar system with a neutron-star component could still exist but with considerably reduced probability. In contrast, models based on direct collapse produce neutron-stars with large radii, often resulting in the neutron-star's demise during a brief, highly radiative phase that typically results in heavy black-holes rather than electromagnetic signals. Consequently, core-collapse physics play a crucial role in multi-messenger astronomy, although further observations are necessary to refine these models and refine electromagnetic production models near the critical mass ratio of 1.32 solar masses.

A previously reported finding from the research of the 1990s and 2000s is the strikingly uniform value of the ratio of variations to the mean in the energy density of quantum fields across various spacetime settings. Initially calculated using correlators of quantum field stress-energy tensors, the issue will now be re-examined using quantum thermodynamics. This is accomplished by determining the thermodynamic quantities known as heat capacity and quantum compressibility in model spacetimes filled with a quantum field at both high and low temperatures. The proportion of these fluctuations to the mean value determines the validity of specific probability distributions. Calculating the free energy density allows the derivation of these quantities. The study utilizes path integrals over compactified, uniform quantum field spacetimes to obtain exact plane-loop and absolute-loop contributions. The results indicate that the statistical distribution of energy density variations converges to the Gaussian type.

Current deep learning techniques used for removing rain from images have achieved notable success in processing artificially created rainy images.  Nonetheless, their effectiveness drastically drops when confronted with genuine rainy conditions, primarily because they often employ highly simplified models of rain which contrast with the complex real rain scenarios.  This study posits that rain simulation and elimination are mutually interconnected and hence need to be inextricably linked.  To accomplish this, a joint approach to learning real rain simulation and elimination within an integrated disentangled image transformation framework is proposed.  A proposed model involves bidirectional translation of disentangled images in two directions: the translation of real rain images into clear backgrounds, coupled with synthetic rain images.  Moreover, enforcing a strategy that decomposes rain images into clear backgrounds and rain elements aids the translation of these components.  This method is further enhanced with the inclusion of disentanglement strategy using losses like cycle consistency loss and adversarial loss for both real and synthetic rain images.  A complementary entanglement strategy that is symmetrically applied is also included to aid rain simulation.  Comprehensive experiments conducted on datasets of artificial and actual rainy conditions demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms other competing techniques.

A prominent paradigm in reward learning utilizes human feedback via comparative evaluations, but their broader adoption is hindered by the expense and labor intensity of these comparisons. To overcome this limitation, we propose grouping multiple comparisons together and allowing human labelers to mark sub-regions of a condensed state space representation, thereby efficiently leveraging human time. Through data visualization techniques, we create an interactive interface for users to label these regions, thereby effectively enhancing the learning agents' performance, even when human labeling time remains constant, across basic Mujoco tasks.

We discuss recent research findings regarding model companions in set theory within the context of ongoing debates in the philosophy of mathematics. Initially, we explore how the concept of model companions is affected by the signature, before specifically examining the dependence of model companions in set theory. Our analysis indicates that the most intrinsic model companions for set theory correspond to $H_{\kappa^+}$ theories, as the infinite cardinal $\kappa$ varies. Furthermore, we highlight that the Continuum problem has a singular solution of $2^{\aleph_0}=\aleph_2$, which aligns with some model companion of enriched set theory containing large cardinal axioms. This model-theoretic framework is justified by a maximality concept reminiscent of Hilbert's axiom of completeness.
This study establishes conditions and proof of existence for a modified Branson-Paneitz equation under Navier boundary conditions on a finite region of n-dimensional Euclidean space.

Evaluating a person's risk of drug abuse is crucial, and online surveys have proven effective for gathering relevant data. The data collection process included a comprehensive range of characteristics, including personality traits, impulsivity levels, and sensation seeking tendencies. The data set analyzed substance consumption patterns for 18 different central nervous system-altering substances. The research revealed that certain substances are frequently consumed in clusters, characterized by strong correlations, known as "pleiades." Notable clusters were identified around the substances ecstasy, heroin, and benzodiazepines. By exploring various classification techniques and features, a data-driven approach identified the most effective methods to categorize individuals as users or non-users for each specific substance or cluster. Among the techniques examined, including tree models and probability estimations, a top-performing classifier was chosen for each drug. The accuracy of these classifications exceeded 70 percent for nearly all substances when using a rigorous evaluation method. The best performance was seen for the substances cannabis, cocaine, ecstasy, LSD, and methanol, achieving a high classification accuracy of above 80 percent.

Our proposed dataset, ATOMIC, is an exhaustive collection of everyday commonsense reasoning rules comprising nearly a million text-based descriptions.  This atlas of inferential knowledge, structured as conditional relationships (if X, then Y), stands out from other available datasets that are centered on categorization, by providing a framework that accounts for causality and effects, actions versus thoughts, and intentional versus unintentional actions.  We have developed nine categories of these relationships and demonstrated the efficacy of incorporating these patterns into models of artificial intelligence.
